items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 46d0bf208e855dc7be381e2cd69e97b1c4dc54c7, which moves state to a dedicated workflow-only branch and makes the run two-phase — commit and verify the history push first, post to chat only afterwards, failing loudly with nothing announced on a rejected push — building on the review-response batch in commit 470c62a37ea2f625611ea07eb7d5fec56f441147.
items.description: The weekly announcement can fire without the pick ever being durably recorded: the script posts to the chat channel before the history file is written, and this workflow step then pushes the history commit straight to the protected default branch with no rebase, retry, or push-success check. The concurrency group only serializes the rotation against itself, so a branch-protection rejection of the automation token or a non-fast-forward race with an ordinary merge leaves the announcement sent but history unrecorded — the next run reads stale history, fairness never advances, and a reroll cannot exclude the current holder.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 470c62a37ea2f625611ea07eb7d5fec56f441147: the pick function now returns a no-op signal, a repeat rotate skips the chat post entirely, and the README wording was aligned.
items.description: A repeat rotate run is a no-op at the history level but returns no signal, and the entry point posts to the chat channel unconditionally outside dry-run — so a manual re-dispatch after the weekly cron re-announces the same person to the team channel; the quiet-diff check suppresses only the duplicate commit, not the post. The README documents rotate as a no-op when the week is already assigned, so behavior and documentation disagree.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 470c62a37ea2f625611ea07eb7d5fec56f441147, which extracts the message builder into its own exported module and covers each mode's label plus the user-mention and team markers.
items.description: The pure function that renders the user-visible chat message — selecting the label per rotation mode and embedding the user-mention markup and team name — is unexported and has no test coverage. A regression such as a reroll rendering the regular-week wording or broken mention markup would be user-visible and permanent in the channel.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 470c62a37ea2f625611ea07eb7d5fec56f441147: the variable-name regex is word-boundary anchored, and a missing or renamed variable (or an empty parse) now throws instead of silently collapsing the pool.
items.description: When extracting member emails from the infrastructure variables file, a renamed variable produces no regex match and the loop silently continues past it. If every declared variable fails to match, the extracted email set collapses to empty and the drift check reports every real roster member as departed — indistinguishable from genuine drift. The unanchored variable-name regex can additionally match a superstring variable name.

items.acceptance_evidence: Fixed by commit 470c62a37ea2f625611ea07eb7d5fec56f441147, which adds not-found, missing-person, and case-insensitive name-match assignment tests.
items.description: The only explicit-assignment test resolves a member by exact-case chat id, so the member-resolution error paths — missing person and unknown person, each with its own thrown message — plus name-based matching and case-insensitivity are never exercised, even though assignment is user-driven through an environment variable.

items.acceptance_evidence: Accepted for the helper: commit 470c62a37ea2f625611ea07eb7d5fec56f441147 covers the three error branches with a mocked fetch; entry-point orchestration coverage followed in commit 1758501035af6e20a814590071129d50c6ee3be4.
items.description: The chat-post helper's error branches — a failed response, a success payload missing the message timestamp, and a payload that is not the expected shape — are non-trivial and mockable but have no test coverage; the entry point's orchestration seam (dry-run, missing token, invalid mode, empty roster, post-then-persist ordering) is likewise uncovered.

items.acceptance_evidence: Accepted and applied in commit 470c62a37ea2f625611ea07eb7d5fec56f441147: the guide-document link lost its edit-mode suffix when the message builder moved into its own module.
items.description: The constant holding the link to the shared guide document ends with an edit-mode path suffix, steering everyone who follows the announcement into the document's editing view rather than a plain read view; the suffix can simply be dropped.
